edits.text: Keep a numeral or quantifier token (digits or spelled-out) together with the immediately following unit/measurement token that completes the numeric expression — including adjacent percent or currency markers and parenthesised unit equivalents.
- Keep a clause‑initial single-word determiner or pronoun together with the immediately following lexical head (the noun or finite verb it introduces).

- As a last resort, order candidate cuts on the source surface as follows: prefer a cut that keeps a numeral or quantifier adjacent to its immediately following unit/measurement token (including percent, currency markers, or parenthetic equivalents) over a cut that keeps a finite verb or auxiliary together with its immediate core complement; prefer either of those over a cut at a punctuation or clause boundary.

- As a last resort, order candidate cuts on the source surface as follows: prefer a cut that keeps a clause‑initial single‑word determiner or pronoun together with its immediate lexical head (noun or finite verb) over a cut that keeps a numeral or quantifier with its immediately following unit/measurement (including %, currency, or a parenthetic unit), over a cut that keeps a finite verb or auxiliary with its immediate core complement; prefer any of these over a cut solely at a punctuation or clause boundary.
